title: The Kitchen of Sandpiper Point
premise: Cyrus Villalobos, a widowed single father running Sandpiper Point's last bookshop, agrees to a fake date with Marisol Reyes—the estranged daughter of the developer threatening to buy out the town's bakery block—to survive his meddling family's reunion. What begins as mutual convenience deepens as Cyrus discovers Marisol is secretly the anonymous investor behind the buyout, torn between loyalty to her father and the truth about what she wants. When the bakery lease deadline forces her deception into the open, Cyrus must decide whether love can survive being built on a lie, and Marisol must forgive herself before she can ask him to. In the end, she publicly kills the development deal, Cyrus forgives her at the reunion where they first pretended, and together they reopen the bakery as a bookshop-café—choosing found family over blood loyalty.
about_author: Tamsin Quintana spent a decade managing a coastal bookshop in Northern California before turning to writing full-time, where she developed a reputation for warm, food-scented small-town romances. She lives with her partner and an ill-tempered cat named Hemingway, and still judges towns by the quality of their bakeries.

chapters.title: The Reunion Clause
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. Cornered by his mother's ultimatum—bring a date to the Villalobos reunion or endure twenty questions about his widowhood—Cyrus impulsively asks Marisol Reyes, the newcomer he's seen arguing with zoning maps outside the bakery. She surprises him by saying yes. The beat: reluctant hope disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: Salt Air and Small Lies
chapters.summary: Marisol POV. At the reunion, their fake chemistry works too well; Cyrus's daughter Lucia adores her, and Marisol feels the first crack in her armor. We glimpse her hidden folder of property documents for 'Meridian Group.' The beat: warmth arriving uninvited.

chapters.title: Second Helpings
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A real second date—unplanned—at the bakery's Sunday market. They share histories: Cyrus's grief, Marisol's years abroad repairing her father's deals. Neither mentions the lease expiring in six weeks. The beat: intimacy outrunning honesty.

chapters.title: The Man Who Owns the Town
chapters.summary: Marisol POV. Her father Emilio arrives in Sandpiper Point, expecting his silent partner to close the acquisition. Marisol stalls, discovering the deal would demolish the bakery—and Cyrus's bookshop sits on the same parcel. The beat: loyalty beginning to curdle.

chapters.title: What Lucia Saw
chapters.summary: Lucia POV (interlude). The sharp-eyed ten-year-old spots Marisol meeting a surveyor behind the bakery and innocently tells her father. Cyrus confronts Marisol gently; she lies badly. He chooses to believe her anyway. The beat: trust extended past its evidence.

chapters.title: Flour, Ash
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. Cyrus finds Meridian's letterhead in Marisol's abandoned tote—her name listed as principal investor. He walks out mid-dinner without a scene, then can't sleep. Meanwhile the bakery owner announces the lease won't be renewed. The beat: heartbreak sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Person in the Mirror
chapters.summary: Marisol POV. Alone, Marisol faces how she became her father: justifying harm as inheritance. She drafts a resignation from Meridian, then goes to the empty bookshop after hours to confess everything to Cyrus—not to be forgiven, but to stop hiding. The beat: self-forgiveness preceding apology.

chapters.title: Deadline
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Lease-signing day. Marisol publicly withdraws Meridian's offer at the town council meeting, burning her relationship with her father. Cyrus watches, unmoved by the gesture alone—but Lucia, present, defends Marisol. The beat: climax; truth costs everything except what matters.

chapters.title: Dessert, For Real This Time
chapters.summary: Cyrus POV. At the family reunion's final night, Cyrus invites Marisol back—not as a fake date but as herself, letting his mother's interrogation land on someone choosing to stay. Father and daughter reconcile partially offstage; forgiveness is offered, not yet complete. The beat: chosen family formed.

chapters.title: The Kitchen of Sandpiper Point
chapters.summary: Marisol POV, epilogue. Six months later: the bakery reopens as a bookshop-café co-run by Cyrus and Marisol, Lucia shelving paperbacks between trays of conchas. Emilio sends a quiet olive branch—a framed photo of the old family kitchen. The beat: second chances, finally well-timed.
